'''Nguyễn Đình Ngọc''' (13 August 1932 – 2 May 2006) was a Vietnamese [[People's Army of Vietnam|Army]] intelligence officer, later a general, and a [[mathematician]].

==Biography==
Nguyễn Đình Ngọc was born in Phượng Dực commune, [[Phú Xuyên District]], [[Hanoi]], [[Vietnam]]. In 1953, he joined the Intelligence Service and served in the [[Vietminh]] Army in the field of public security.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://congluan.vn/vi-tuong-cham-chan-30-phut-post77130.html|title = Vị tướng chậm chân 30 phút|date = 29 April 2020}}</ref> He was then assigned to [[Saigon]] to work as a spy for [[North Vietnam]] (officially known as the Democratic Republic of Vietnam). In 1955, he moved to [[France]] to complete his studies after being awarded a scholarship. He attended the [[University of Paris]], from which he graduated with three engineering degrees: Hydrology and Meteorology, Shipbuilding and Telecommunications. Additionally, he earned a [[Ph.D.]] in [[Geography]]{{citation needed|date=March 2025}} and in [[Mathematics]], under the supervision of [[Charles Ehresmann]], with a thesis entitled "Sur les espaces fibres et les prolongements" (On [[fiber bundle]]s and prolongations) at the Paris-Sorbonne University in 1963.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|98579}}</ref>

==Activity==

In 1966, Ngọc returned to [[Vietnam]] where he was assigned the task of managing and developing the public telecommunications in the field of [[information security]] and technology for [[South Vietnam]] (officially known as Republic of Vietnam), while teaching mathematics at the Saigon University of Science and at various colleges in South Vietnam, as told by himself in an autobiographical article.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.math.hcmus.edu.vn/giới-thiệu/2-tài-nguyên/21-tình-hình-toán-học-ở-miền-nam-trước-1975 | title=Tình hình Toán học ở Miền Nam trước 1975 | date=25 September 2019 }}</ref> At the same time he was a communist spy who sent important information to the North.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://congluan.vn/vi-tuong-cham-chan-30-phut-post77130.html|title = Vị tướng chậm chân 30 phút|date = 29 April 2020}}</ref> After the [[Fall of Saigon]] and reunification of Vietnam on 30 April 1975, he helped developing the computer and telecommunication for the [[Socialist Republic of Vietnam]]'s government. He also studied and accessed the computers provided by [[Soviet Union]] and other communist countries.

In 1989 Ngọc joined a newly established [[Thang Long University]] - a private university in [[Hanoi]]. He is a founder of the [[Radio and Electronics Association of Vietnam]] and the [[Informatics Association of Vietnam]]. In 1994 he was promoted to [[Major general]] of [[Vietnam People's Public Security]] (police and security forces).<ref>{{cite web | url=http://cand.com.vn/Guong-sang/Thieu-tuong-GS-TSKH-Nguyen-Dinh-Ngoc-Vinh-quang-la-lang-le-19464/ | title=Thiếu tướng, GS, TSKH Nguyễn Đình Ngọc: Vinh quang là lặng lẽ }}</ref>

== Death ==
He died of cancer on May 2, 2006 at the hospital 198 (Ministry of Public Security).
